# Sirach Chapter 30 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 30 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**30:1** He who loves his son will keep on chastising him, so that he may rejoice over him at the end and not grieve before his neighbors.

**30:2** He who disciplines his son will profit from him and will boast of him among his acquaintances.

**30:3** He who educates his son will make his enemy envious, and before his friends he will rejoice over him.

**30:4** The father dies, and it is as though he has not died; for he has left behind one like himself.

**30:5** In his lifetime he saw him and rejoiced over him, and at death he was not grieved.

**30:6** Against his enemies he left behind an avenger, and toward his friends one who returns kindness.

**30:7** He who coddles his son will bind up his wounds, and at every outcry his heart will be shaken.

**30:8** An unbroken horse turns stubborn, and a son left to himself turns headstrong.

**30:9** Pamper your child and he will terrify you; play with him and he will bring you grief.

**30:10** Do not laugh with him, lest you have to weep with him; and in the end you will gnash your teeth.

**30:11** Do not give him freedom in his youth, and do not ignore his follies.

**30:12** Bow down his neck in his youth and beat his sides while he is still young, lest he become stubborn and refuse to obey you, and there will be grief to your soul.

**30:13** Discipline your son and labor over him, lest his shameful behavior cause you to stumble.

**30:14** Better is a poor man who is healthy and strong in body than a rich man whose flesh is afflicted.

**30:15** Health and soundness of body are better than all gold, and a vigorous body than boundless wealth.

**30:16** There is no wealth better than health of body, and there is no pleasure better than joy of heart.

**30:17** Death is better than a bitter life, and eternal rest better than chronic illness.

**30:18** Good things poured before a mouth that is closed are like offerings placed in front of a tomb.

**30:19** What benefit is an offering to an idol? For it cannot eat or smell. So too the one who is punished by the LORD —

**30:20** seeing with his eyes and groaning, as a eunuch who embraces a virgin and sighs.

**30:21** Do not give yourself over to sorrow, and do not torment yourself in your own deliberation.

**30:22** Gladness of heart is a man's life, and the joy of a man is length of days.

**30:23** Console yourself and give your heart cheer; and drive away sorrow from yourself, for sorrow has destroyed many, and there is no benefit in it.

**30:24** Envy and anger shorten life, and worry brings on premature old age.

**30:25** A cheerful and good heart will take care in its food, and his meals he will give proper attention.
